title: Culture and Heritages in India-I: Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism
summary: A visit to a holy place is a tirtha (river ford, place of pilgrimage) and the journey is tirtha-yatra. Adi Shankaracharya established four mathas in the 8th century in the four corners of India: Badrinath (north), Dwarka (west), Puri (east) and Sringeri (south, Karnataka; Kanchi is also mentioned). The four Dhams are Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri and Rameshwaram.

Dwarka (Gujarat): capital of Krishna's kingdom, main temple Jagat Mandir. Puri: Lord Jagannath with Balram and Subhadra; the annual Rath Yatra to the Gundicha temple draws a mass of devotees and foreign tourists. Sringeri: on the Tunga river, deity Saraswati (Sharada), non-sectarian, fishes handfed at the ghats. Badrinath (Uttarakhand): home of Lord Vishnu, on the Alaknanda, deity of black stone, hot spring, open May to October; the pilgrims cry 'Jai Badri Vishal'; Lakshmi took the form of a badri tree to shelter Vishnu. Varanasi (Kashi): the most sacred, city of Shiva with over two thousand temples, a centre of learning (Bernier called it the Athens of India) where Hindus wish to die for moksha. Gaya: rituals for ancestors' moksha. Haridwar: 'Gateway of the Ganga' where it enters the plains (Hari ka dwar, Mayapur). Ayodhya: Rama's city. Kanchipuram: 14 of the 108 Vishnu temples; sacred to Saivites and Vaishnavites. Kedarnath: remotest of the Char Dham on the Mandakini; named for King Kedar. Somnath (Gujarat): one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, 'the Shrine Eternal'. Amarnath (Jammu and Kashmir): ice Shivling cave; annual pilgrimage in summer. Kamakhya (Guwahati): 'renowned goddess of desire', a Shakti Peetha. Mount Kailash: home of Shiva, 6,714 m, in the south-west of Tibet. Mathura and Vrindavan: Brajbhoomi, birthplace of Krishna on the Yamuna; Holi and Janmashtami. Nashik: Rama's residence in exile. Prayag (Allahabad): meeting of Ganga and Yamuna, Kumbh Mela. Rameshwaram: tip of the Indian peninsula, where Rama built the bridge to Sri Lanka. Ujjain (Shipra, Avanti), Pushkar (only temple of Brahma), Tirupati Balaji (richest temple) and Vaishno Devi (Trikuta mountains, 60 km from Jammu).

Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara, was born at Vaishali, left home at 30, meditated 12 years, became the Jina (conqueror) and died at Pawapuri at 72 in 527 BCE. Teachings: no belief in God, yagnas or caste, equality of all; four vows (non-violence, truth, non-possession, non-stealing); the threefold path of Right Belief, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct leading to moksha (Siddha Sila); the principle of ahimsa. He preached in Ardha Magadhi (Prakrit). Sects: Digambaras (sky-clad) and Shwetambaras (white-clad). Magadha rulers Bimbisara and Ajatashatru patronised it.

Jain sites: Mount Parsvanatha (Sametshikhar, Bihar) where twenty of the twenty-four Tirthankaras attained moksha; Pawapuri (Bihar; Diwali marks Mahavira's nirvana); Jaisalmer (library of manuscripts, yellow-stone temples); Ranakpur (Rajasthan, 15th century, 1,444 pillars, four statues of Rishabha); Dilwara temples on Mount Abu (white marble, delicate carving; Vimala Shah's temple of about 1030, Tejapala's Neminatha temple of about 1230); Girnar (Gujarat, temple city, where Neminatha attained moksha); Shatrunjaya (Gujarat, first Tirthankara Rishabha, hundreds of temples); Shravanabelagola (Karnataka, the 57-ft monolithic statue of Bahubali, about 980 CE, the biggest free-standing monolithic statue in the world, anointed every 12–15 years in the Mahamastakabhisheka).

Gautama Buddha (Shakya tribe) was born at Lumbini near Kapilavastu in 567 BCE, left home after seeing an old man, a sick man and a dead man, was enlightened under the pipal (Bodhi) tree at Bodh Gaya, gave his first sermon at the Deer Park, Sarnath and attained Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar at 80. Teachings: desire is the cause of suffering; the Eightfold Path of right conduct (view), speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness, meditation and resolution leads to nirvana. He preached in Pali and Prakrit. Sanghas and viharas grew and universities such as Nalanda developed.

Buddhist sites: Sarnath (Dhamekh Stupa, Ashokan pillar); Sanchi (Great Stupa founded by Ashoka; toranas added by the Satavahanas); Amravati and Bharhut stupas; Nagarjunakonda; Harwan; Ajanta caves (murals, found by a British army officer in 1819); Nalanda (4th–12th century seat of learning, 2,000 teachers and 10,000 students, Hiuen Tsang studied there); Udaygiri (Odisha, Vajrayana centre); Bodh Gaya (Mahabodhi Temple); Rajgir (Buddha spent 12 years; capital of Magadha); Vaishali; monasteries at McLeod Ganj (Dalai Lama's temple), Ki, Tabo (over 1,000 years old), Rumtek (Sikkim) and Ghoom.

vsa: Describe any two points of significance of Kedarnath as a popular destination for Hindu pilgrims.
It is the remotest of the Char Dham sites, on the Mandakini river near the Chorabari glacier in the Himalayas. Its temple is one of the holiest Hindu temples and is named after King Kedar.

or: Describe any two points of significance of Nalanda as an important centre of Buddhists.
It was an ancient seat of Buddhist learning from the 4th to 12th century with 2,000 teachers and 10,000 students. Hiuen Tsang studied there and praised its education.

vsa: Describe the main sects of Jainism.
Jainism has two sects: the Digambaras (sky-clad, wear no clothes) and the Shwetambaras (wear white clothes).
October 2025

or: Why is the Jain temple at Mount Abu in Rajasthan famous? Explain in two points.
The Dilwara temples are masterpieces of Jain architecture built in white marble with delicate carving. They were built by Vimala Shah (about 1030) and Tejapala (about 1230).

vsa: Describe any two characteristics of Udaygiri as a holy place for Buddhists.
It is a Buddhist site in Odisha dating from the 6th century. In the 8th century it was an important centre of Vajrayana art and philosophy.
April 2024
Describe the three main teachings of Lord Mahavira.
He preached non-violence (ahimsa), truth and non-possession and non-stealing as the four vows. He taught the threefold path of right belief, knowledge and conduct and equality of all people.
October 2025
Describe the sacred value of Mathura in any two points.
Mathura is the birthplace of Lord Krishna on the Yamuna and is known as Brajbhoomi. Holi and Janmashtami draw pilgrims and tourists to Mathura and Vrindavan.
October 2025
State the four vows taught by Mahavira.
Not to injure life, not to tell lies, not to own property and not to steal.
What is the Eightfold Path of Buddhism?
It is the path of right view, resolution, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and meditation (conduct) that removes desire and leads to nirvana.
Name the four mathas established by Adi Shankaracharya.
Badrinath in the north, Dwarka in the west, Puri in the east and Sringeri in the south.
What is Rath Yatra? Where is it held?
It is the annual festival at Puri when the idols of Jagannath, Balram and Subhadra are taken in raths to the Gundicha temple and brought back after some days.
Why is Bodh Gaya important for Buddhists?
Buddha attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree here, and it is one of the four most sacred Buddhist sites. The Mahabodhi Temple stands here.
sa: Explain any three Jain heritage sites located in Rajasthan.

(i) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu, built in white marble with fine carving. (ii) Ranakpur temple (15th century) with 1,444 carved pillars and four marble statues of Rishabha. (iii) Jaisalmer, with intricately carved yellow-stone temples and a famous library of Jain manuscripts.
Explain the significance of Amarnath as a holy place of Hindus.

(i) It is a cave shrine of Lord Shiva in Jammu and Kashmir surrounded by snowy mountains. (ii) It is open to pilgrims only for a short period in summer. (iii) Lakhs of pilgrims make an annual trek to see the ice Shivling.
Explain any three points of significance of Shravanabelagola as a holy place for Jains.

(i) It has the 57-ft monolithic statue of Bahubali carved about 980 CE, the biggest free-standing monolithic statue in the world. (ii) It stands on a hill reached by about five hundred steps. (iii) Every 12 to 15 years the Mahamastakabhisheka is held when the statue is showered from scaffolding.
Describe the sacred value of Banaras (Varanasi) for Hindus in three points.

(i) It is the most sacred city, the city of Shiva, with over two thousand temples. (ii) It is on the Ganga and Hindus wish to die here to attain moksha. (iii) It was a great centre of learning, called the Athens of India by Bernier.
Describe the religious heritage values of Dwarka, Puri and Somnath.
(i) Dwarka was the capital of Krishna's kingdom with Jagat Mandir. (ii) Puri has the Jagannath temple and the Rath Yatra. (iii) Somnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, known as the Shrine Eternal.
Explain any three Buddhist heritage sites in India.

(i) Sarnath, where Buddha preached the first sermon, has the Dhamekh Stupa and Ashokan pillar. (ii) Bodh Gaya has the Mahabodhi Temple where he was enlightened. (iii) Sanchi's Great Stupa, founded by Ashoka, has fine toranas.
la: Write an essay on the life and teachings of Vardhamana Mahavira, in six points.

(i) He was the 24th Tirthankara, born at Vaishali to Siddhartha, a Kshatriya clan chief. (ii) At thirty he left home and meditated for twelve years until he became the Jina. (iii) He rejected belief in God, yagnas and the caste system and taught equality. (iv) He taught four vows: not to injure life, tell lies, own property or steal. (v) The threefold path of right belief, knowledge and conduct leads to moksha, and ahimsa is the central principle. (vi) He preached in Ardha Magadhi (Prakrit), Jainism later split into Digambaras and Shwetambaras and he died at Pawapuri at 72.
Who was the founder of Buddhism? Explain the teachings of Buddha in six points.

(i) Gautama Buddha, born at Lumbini in 567 BCE, founded Buddhism. (ii) Seeing an old man, a sick man and a dead man, he left home and was enlightened at Bodh Gaya. (iii) He gave his first sermon at Sarnath. (iv) He taught that desire is the cause of suffering. (v) He taught the Eightfold Path of right view, resolution, speech, action, livelihood, effort, mindfulness and meditation. (vi) He preached in Pali and Prakrit and stressed morality and virtue; the Sangha and viharas spread his teachings.
Discuss Hindu religious heritage sites in India in six points.

(i) The four mathas and Dhams: Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri and Rameshwaram (and Sringeri). (ii) Varanasi, the city of Shiva and moksha. (iii) Haridwar, Prayag (Kumbh Mela) and Ayodhya. (iv) Mathura and Vrindavan, the land of Krishna. (v) Kedarnath, Amarnath, Somnath and Mount Kailash for Shiva. (vi) Vaishno Devi, Tirupati Balaji, Kamakhya and Pushkar.
Discuss the major Jain heritage sites of India, in six points.

(i) Mount Parsvanatha in Bihar, where twenty Tirthankaras attained moksha. (ii) Pawapuri, where Mahavira attained nirvana. (iii) Dilwara temples at Mount Abu in white marble. (iv) Ranakpur with 1,444 carved pillars. (v) Girnar and Shatrunjaya in Gujarat. (vi) Shravanabelagola with the 57-ft Bahubali statue.
